transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-12-01
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Julian (Redwood SE), Lena (Sylvan Platform), Marcus (Sylvan SRE), Priya (Sylvan Security)

Summary: (auto) quick walkthrough of tenant governance features, org/project token models, and policies. Customer curious about handling bursty traffic from internal teams and compliance exports.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Julian SE here to run the console demo. Could folks say their roles?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Lena): Hi, Lena Cho, platform eng, we run a multi-tenant API for clients and internal services.
00:18 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Marcus, SRE, we own capacity and SLAs.
00:22 Speaker 4 (Priya): Priya Nair, security, SOC 2 and KMS questions mostly.
00:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Agenda — org vs project keys, rate-sculpting, sticky routing to Dedicated pools, RBAC and audit logs. Any must-have topics? Marcus?
00:44 Speaker 3 (Marcus): We need to keep latencies under 120ms p95 for the realtime endpoint; but costs are ballooning. Also want predictable degradation if we hit bursts.
00:56 Speaker 2 (Julian): Perfect, we built the demo around that — we'll show a policy that preserves p95 by shifting noncritical traffic to a cheaper model or dedicated burst lane.
01:10 Speaker 2 (Julian): Jumping into Console — top left "Organizations" list, we pick Sylvan-Prod org. You can see org-level quotas and then project slices. Note the blue "rate-sculpt" policy example.
01:35 Speaker 2 (Julian): So org keys are great for cross-team visibility but not ideal for per-team throttles. We recommend project keys per internal team; they map to Project objects and can have independent quotas and sticky routing.
01:58 Speaker 4 (Priya): Quick Q: Does a project key ever inherit org-level retention settings? We have data residency constraints in EU region, need KMS integration.
02:12 Speaker 2 (Julian): Short answer yes — policies cascade. You can pin a project to regional pools, and we support customer-managed keys via KMS; I'll show the security panel later.
02:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): On quotas — the rate-sculpting policy lets you define slices: baseline qps, burst bucket, and a secondary lane that routes to Dedicated or cheaper open model when over threshold.
02:46 Speaker 3 (Marcus): How's backpressure handled? We can't have queue pileups on the edge.
02:53 Speaker 2 (Julian): We do token bucket + immediate failover rules. If burst exceeds capacity, preconfigured fallbacks route to a lower-cost model or a queue with explicit retry headers. There's also concurrency guardrails.
03:18 Speaker 2 (Julian): (typing) Here's an example: Team-A project key is limited to 120 rps baseline, with a 500-token burst buffer that triggers sticky routing to "dedicated-burst-1" pool for up to 15s.
03:38 Speaker 2 (Julian): Note the "stickiness window" — after a project is routed to a pool, subsequent requests within N seconds stay on that pool to preserve KV cache locality.
03:58 Speaker 4 (Priya): That's helpful for latency. What about audit logs? We need per-token traces for compliance.
04:10 Speaker 2 (Julian): Console -> Security -> Audit exports. You can stream per-request metadata to your S3 or SIEM; logs include token id (hashed), route decisions, latency, and model variant.
04:28 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Any limits on how many project keys we create? We have 50+ internal services.
04:35 Speaker 2 (Julian): No hard cap; there are practical UI filters and API pagination. For scale we recommend using org-level provisioning via API so you can create keys programmatically.
04:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): Let's talk Optimize suggestions — for high-throughput teams we recommend prefix caching and batching windows. It can reduce token cost ~30% depending on prompt reuse.
05:06 Speaker 2 (Julian): Also we can recommend quantized variants for low-cost tails, like int8 for analytical workloads, and sticky routing will prefer cheaper variants when latency budgets allow it.
05:22 Speaker 4 (Priya): Are model variants audited for drift? We can't accept silent quality regressions.
05:30 Speaker 2 (Julian): We integrate with Redwood Evals and quality monitors. You can tie prompt sets to rollout policies that block auto-fallback if quality drops beyond thresholds.
05:48 Speaker 3 (Marcus): For our pilot, we want three teams: search, notifications, and analytics. Search needs low latency and dedicated pool; analytics can be cheaper.
06:04 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll propose a pilot topology: org-level billing with three project keys, one dedicated pool for search, sticky routing policies, and rate-sculpting for notifications.
06:20 Speaker 2 (Julian): Quick note: if you want absolute isolation for search, choose Dedicated capacity with reserved GPUs — that gives capacity guarantees but costs more.
06:36 Speaker 4 (Priya): On encryption, can we use our HSM for key wrapping?
06:42 Speaker 2 (Julian): Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations; some enterprises prefer customer-managed key wrapping — that's in our Private deployment notes.
06:54 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Performance test — can you run a small benchmark with our 95th latency target and show fallbacks? We'll supply an endpoint and token map.
07:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Julian will run a smoke benchmark. Julian, we'll need a simple load script and guidance for headers.
07:14 Speaker 2 (Julian): I'll provide a JMeter/Postman script, and a small harness that toggles project key rates and shows routing decisions in the trace logs.
07:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): Any blockers? Priya?
07:32 Speaker 4 (Priya): We need SOC2 artifacts and an inventory of data flows for legal. Also, can we see retention policy controls per project?
07:44 Speaker 2 (Julian): Yes — retention is per-project; you can set automatic purges and export windows. We'll attach the documentation.
07:58 Speaker 3 (Marcus): One more — can routing policies be tag-driven (e.g., route all "canary" tag traffic to cheaper models)?
08:06 Speaker 2 (Julian): Yes, routing supports request-level metadata matching: tags, header values, and organizational attributes.
08:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): Ok let's summarize next steps and owners.
08:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): Action items and follow ups: we'll send pilot pricing, trial org, security pack. Julian will prep benchmark harness. Priya will share compliance checklist. Marcus will provide SLOs and sample workload.
08:46 Speaker 4 (Priya): Thanks, this was helpful — one note, the UI had a typo in "stickness window" earlier, haha.
08:55 Speaker 2 (Julian): (laughs) noted, we'll report that.
09:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll target the benchmark next Wed. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript (approx 54 minutes).
